findings.title: Completed deviation, continuing consequence
findings.claim: The perfect intransitive ḍalla marks the straying condition as entered; the matching imperfect yaḍillu carries deviation into an ongoing result, with alayha placing its harm on the self.
findings.mechanism: The perfect protasis and imperfect result share d-l-l but differ in aspect. The earlier h-d-y path supplies an independent directional pole, and the upon-it phrase returns the adverse yield to the actor. The branch for loss adds a qualified lost-path pressure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see both a choice already taken and the continuing cost of its direction.
findings.containment: Form I remains intransitive moral deviation, not causing another to stray. Lost-path pressure is a secondary analogy, not literal disappearance or an unavenged loss. Later-ayah references in the source are outside the selected context.

epistemic.reason: Aspect, intransitivity, and the local path contrast are directly supported; the loss facet is analogical and bounded.

findings.containment: The clause concerns carrying another's burden; it does not prohibit assistance in other forms.

epistemic.reason: The supplied mood and adjacent syntax distinguish negation from prohibition.

findings.containment: The local verb selects carrying liability. Refuge, military equipment, and ministerial roles remain available root branches without a focus trigger; cited formula recurrences are outside this packet.

epistemic.reason: The triple root chain, negation, and other-owner phrase directly support the load reading and its responsibility extension.

findings.title: Guidance continues in the result
findings.claim: Yahtadi places guidance in an ongoing imperfect result after ihtada has marked entry into the condition.
findings.mechanism: The perfect and imperfect forms repeat the same root across protasis and apodosis, making the result an ongoing consequence of the completed entry; li-nafsi identifies its beneficiary.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a path entered and then continuing as benefit for the actor.
findings.containment: The clause has no overt path object; the self phrase marks beneficiary rather than naming a physical destination.

epistemic.reason: The aspect pattern and beneficiary relation are focus-local.

findings.title: Guidance directed for the self
findings.claim: Li marks the guided result as benefit for the self, while the later alayha phrase sets straying against that same self.
findings.mechanism: The first preposition gives the result a beneficiary relation; the focus-local second preposition supplies a contrasting adverse relation with a feminine pronoun.
findings.reader_payoff: The paired prepositions turn moral outcomes into two differently directed relations to the same actor.
findings.containment: The contrast is supplied by this ayah's own two clauses and does not rely on a neighboring ayah.

epistemic.reason: Both prepositions and their self references are present in the focus surface.

findings.title: The accountable self
findings.claim: Nafsihi identifies the actor's own accountable self as the beneficiary, and the later alayha phrase returns the adverse result to that self.
findings.mechanism: The possessed self occurs after li in the guidance result; the paired feminine pronoun on alayha then meets the independent burden boundary at ukhra, keeping self and other distinct.
findings.reader_payoff: The actor is the point where benefit and harm terminate, while another person's load remains separately owned.
findings.containment: The local referent is the accountable self. Breath, body, and other n-f-s branches have no independent trigger here; references to 17:14 and 17:7 are not used.

epistemic.reason: Possession, beneficiary syntax, the repeated self reference, and the other-owner phrase are supplied.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bir şeyin bütün gerçeği ve öz varlığıyla kendisini pekiştirerek gösterir.
branch_activations.carrier: Nafsihi carries the local possessed-self sense.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The later upon-it phrase returns harm to the same referent, and ukhra names a separate person.
branch_activations.activation: The self phrase meets a parallel return and a distinct other-owner boundary.

branch_activations.boundary: The branch does not activate breath, body, appetite, or an immaterial-soul claim.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Kişinin başkası aracılığıyla değil, bizzat kendisinin bulunmasını belirtir.
branch_activations.carrier: The possessed self is named as the beneficiary of guidance.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The straying result returns to that self, while the burden clause distinguishes the self from another owner.

findings.title: A paired alternative
findings.claim: The wa coordinates straying as a second condition parallel to guidance, not as an effect that follows from it.
findings.mechanism: The coordinator stands between two man protases, each with its own result connector and restricted outcome.
findings.reader_payoff: Guidance and straying remain co-present alternatives under the same open conditional frame.
findings.containment: Coordination pairs the cases without ranking either one's truth or causation.

epistemic.reason: The two protases and their repeated structure are explicit in the focus syntax.

findings.title: The second whoever
findings.claim: The repeated man opens the straying case to the same unrestricted range of actors as the guidance case.
findings.mechanism: The second conditional relator begins its own perfect protasis after wa, preserving formal balance before the parallel fa-result.
findings.reader_payoff: The negative path is an independent possibility for whoever acts, not a consequence assigned only to the first group.
findings.containment: The matching form supports parallel scope; it does not make guidance and straying equivalent outcomes.

epistemic.reason: The repeated conditional word and matching clause pattern are directly supplied.

findings.title: Direction returns to the chooser
findings.claim: The paired guidance and straying clauses turn two opposite directions into yields that return to each chooser's own self: guidance gathers the self onto a course, while deviation carries a qualified lost-path cost.
findings.mechanism: The h-d-y words supply the positive route, d-l-l supplies departure from it, and li-nafsi versus alayha returns each result to the same actor. This changes the simple before-reading of two choices with personal consequences into an ongoing relation between direction and the chooser's own identity.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the path as something entered and the consequence as something borne by the same self, with both guidance and straying remaining live.
findings.containment: The h-d-y and d-l-l branches match supplied focus words; the d-l-l loss facet remains a qualified path/self-cost analogy. It does not assert a literal lost object, a causative misleader, or an afterlife claim. HFT provenance is legacy_unbound, so the composite model remains attributed rather than independently established by that source alone.

epistemic.reason: The exact coordinates and local word relations are corroborated in the packet, while the integrated before/after model originates in a legacy_unbound HFT record.

findings.title: A load cannot change bearer
findings.claim: The three w-z-r forms make responsibility perceptible as weight attached to its bearer; the negation closes its transfer across the boundary marked by ukhra.
findings.mechanism: The verb of carrying, active participle, and load object repeat one root before categorical la denies cross-person bearing. The helper branch supplies an analogical surrogate relation that the denial closes, while akhra names the distinct owner. This changes the simple before-reading that each person is responsible for personal wrongdoing into the after-reading of identity-tagged weight: support may exist, but substitution fails.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish helping someone from becoming the bearer of that person's accountable load.
findings.containment: The helper reading is an analogy carried by the repeated load relation and negation, not a literal office or proof that help is impossible. The local clause denies burden transfer and leaves other forms of support open; HFT provenance remains legacy_unbound.

epistemic.reason: The root chain, negation, and other-person coordinate are independently supplied; the integrated helper/surrogate relation comes from a legacy_unbound HFT nomination.

findings.title: A notice threshold before punishment
findings.claim: The negated punisher state is procedurally bounded: an address-bearing dispatch must intervene before the punitive state can begin.
findings.mechanism: Kunna supplies a state predicate, muadhdhibina names active punishment, hatta holds that predicate open to nabatha, and rasulan makes the dispatch a messenger rather than the punishment itself. This changes the simple before-reading that punishment does not happen before a messenger arrives into a sequenced threshold between unaddressed persons and punitive action.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees notice and dispatch as the event that closes a waiting interval before punishment.
findings.containment: The sequence is a focus-local reading of the negated predicate and its endpoint. It does not specify message content, determine what counts as adequate notice, or establish a wider legal rule. HFT provenance is legacy_unbound and the supplied ʿ-dh-b branch is qualified.

epistemic.reason: The morphology, threshold syntax, and focus-root branches corroborate the contact; the integrated procedural model is a legacy_unbound HFT nomination.
